title: The Return of the Lunchbox
skyStory: The moon is exactly half lit in Sagittarius, balanced like an archer with an arrow drawn and absolutely no idea where to aim. Summer packs up its folding chairs. The school buses are back on the roads, yellow as ducklings. Somewhere a centaur in the stars is trying to remember its locker combination, and Saturn refuses to help.

reading: The back-to-routine wave hits like cold water on a warm ankle. Calendars fill. Inboxes swell. The cabin's chimney is puffing like an old engine getting back up to speed. You are good at this part, the restart, the rallying. People look to you on mornings like this whether you notice or not.

Around 10:30 am, give someone a pep talk without them knowing it is a pep talk. A quick good morning with real eye contact. A specific compliment on something they made. Life Path 3 was made for exactly this kind of small, warm broadcast. The [[Three of Wands]] sees your ships going out, and every one of them is carrying good words.
joel.mission: Give three specific compliments before noon, each about something someone made or did, never about how they look.
joel.omen: A yellow school bus stopping right in front of you. A lesson from last spring is ready to be used now.

reading: Today you are the person everyone accidentally asks where things are. The stapler. The password. The good scissors. The Wood Rat knows, of course, because the Wood Rat notices where everything goes, even the things other people lose on purpose.

By midafternoon you will have helped six people level up in tiny ways, and you will not count any of it as work. Count it. The [[Page of Pentacles]] is writing it down for you in very neat handwriting. Then save the last hour of the day for one thing only you can do, and do it slowly, the way a mountain does everything.
nancy.mission: Keep a tally of every question you answer today, and announce the final number at dinner like a sports score.
nancy.omen: Someone holding the door for a long time. Help you gave last week is about to come back around.
nancy.elementWhy: the steady one in the storm

together.text: Each of you name one thing you want to have finished by the equinox on the twenty-second. Just one. Write it somewhere you will both see. The archer in the sky is lending you its arrow, and it would like it back eventually, preferably on target.

game.intro: Back-to-school week, and the lunchbox has returned from exile. Pick yours, then guess what the other one grabbed.
game.question: Which lunchbox would ten-year-old you have defended with your whole heart?
